Chapter 1: Practice a Specific Sub-skill or Technique.
You know, when we think about getting better at something, it's tempting to just dive right in and practice the whole thing at once.
But what if you could break it down? Imagine learning to play guitar. Instead of strumming through entire songs and hoping for the best, what if you focused on just one chord, or even a single strumming pattern?
That’s where practicing a specific sub-skill or technique really shines. By narrowing your attention to one small piece, you can master it so much faster.
Think about athletes—like basketball players who spend hours just working on free throws, or runners who zero in on their sprint starts. They’re not practicing the whole game; they’re polishing one tiny part until it feels natural.
Here’s something to pay attention to: when you isolate a sub-skill, you get to focus your energy. You can spot mistakes, fix them right away, and build confidence as you go.
And this works for just about anything—whether you’re learning a language, improving your cooking, or even becoming better at public speaking. Maybe you practice pronunciation for just one tricky word, or you nail down one recipe technique before moving on.
So, next time you’re trying to improve, ask yourself: what’s one small part I can work on right now? Give it your full attention, and don’t rush it.
Mastering those little pieces adds up way faster than you might think.
Ready to try it out? Pick just one sub-skill or technique, and see how much progress you can make.
